method: Intraday momentum with noise bands (Zarattini, Aziz, Barbon 2024), as published: 14-session noise, decisions every 30 minutes, long and short, flat at the close. The average-price line is time-weighted (no volume), so different price feeds give the same signals.
data: 5-minute bars, regular US hours, Alpaca market data
selection_rule: Sharpe after costs above 0.3 on 2016-2021 with instant fills and with fills 5 minutes late

learning.how: Each year is traded with a model fitted only on earlier years' days; it skips a day whose first signal looks like past losing days. Kept only if it beat the plain rules on 2018-2021 and beat filters trained on scrambled outcomes.

fill_speed.data: 1-minute bars (Alpaca): each order is re-priced at the open of the minute N minutes after its signal

futures.note: Tested on each contract's index fund during regular US hours (09:30-16:00 New York) at futures costs. Futures also trade overnight; this method does not. A fund is a close stand-in, not the contract itself. Checked in November 2026 against the real contracts (NQ=F, ES=F) over 35 sessions: the funds' daily results matched theirs with a correlation of 0.99.

rejected_rules: opening-range breakout (first-hour high/low, stop at the other side): -5.8%/yr
first-hour momentum held to the close: -9.3%/yr
last-half-hour momentum: -11.8%/yr (costs alone exceed the edge)
fading the opening gap: -6.7%/yr; following the gap: -4.1%/yr
crypto 24-hour breakout: -16.7%/yr; crypto dip-buying (RSI): -9.2%/yr; crypto hourly trend: -51.5%/yr
adaptive market switch (trade a market only while its own trailing 3-12 month result is positive): +2.5% to +4.2%/yr vs +5.8% for a fixed list
volatility-scaled position size: Sharpe 0.61 vs 0.55, too small to matter
caveats: Simulated on historical data with assumed costs; not real trading.
The edge is thin: it lost money on 20 of the 28 markets tested on unseen data.
It depends on fast, cheap fills: results with fills 1 to 5 minutes late are shown next to the instant ones.
No leverage in the test. Short positions need a margin account; futures need a futures account.
